issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature accepts two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), while the problem statement and UML specify a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int). The solution repository implements addGuestStudents(int) with a single parameter. This parameter mismatch will confuse students about which signature to implement and will cause compilation/test failures if tests expect the single-parameter version.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). Remove the extra boolean parameter (or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to document the additional parameter if it was intended). Ensure the template method stub compiles with the single-parameter signature so students implement the correct method.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect an addGuestStudents method with a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)), but the template defines addGuestStudents(int, boolean). This parameter-signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) creates a mapping confusion for students: they will follow the exercise description expecting addGuestStudents(int) but find a different method signature in the starter code, which may prevent straightforward implementation or testing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ }. If input validation is required, perform it inside that single-parameter method rather than exposing an extra boolean parameter in the signature.
